The PR modifies only lines 11-45 at the top of the file, adding a v0.10.13 candidate section (loop-guard for Gemma 4 thoughts, joining-Mac stop handling, rollout notes). Documentation only: no source, config, key handling, attestation or authorization code changes appear in the supplied evidence. The visible base text does not overlap the changed range, so no cited line is affected. The truncated patch excerpt ends mid-sentence, so I examined only the visible part of the head additions.

Relevant threat areas, noted without a finding: the new text describes behavior changes in the provider. Examples are the Gemma 4 loop guard closing a thought and answering within the request's budget (disabled with logprobs or on a pair, kill switch DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING=0), and the joining Mac ending only on a requested stop, which now ends the leader's start during download or load. The latter touches cluster lifecycle availability (A-018, T-010-like cancellation semantics). The actual implementations (#2040, #2042) are not in the supplied evidence. Any security consequences, such as output-token accounting or stop authorization on the pairing-keyed control channel, must be reviewed in those code changes, not here.

The changelog claims the registration, MLX pins and toolchain are unchanged. These are unverified claims about the signed artifact and qualification (A-017, T-054). They should be confirmed against the release workflow, not the changelog. No security regression, new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumption was identified in the supplied docs-only change.
